lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 101: in split view, Insert drops the selected files on the other pane.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one oh one: in split view, Insert drops the selected files on the other pane.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
You press Insert with focus in the file view, in split view, with files selected.
The new window action skips files already in the other folder and refuses what a drop would refuse.
Then the drop rule, now in its own function, decides between move and copy.
The files go over the way a real drop sends them, and focus stays where it was.
The same action is in the Edit menu, greyed out unless it would really transfer something.
Drag and drop now shares both rules, so its decisions don't change.
Before, moving files across split view took a drag, or Cut, a click and Paste; now one key does it.
Insert has no rule of its own: it shares the drop's move-or-copy code, so the two can't drift apart.
Shift+Insert and Ctrl+Insert were dropped from the issue, because they already paste and copy in Thunar.
lines.say: Shift Insert and Control Insert were dropped from the issue, because they already paste and copy in Thunar.

lines.caption: Insert works only with focus in the file view; in a text field, such as the location bar, it stays a text key.
Files already in the other folder are skipped; if nothing would transfer, the key goes on.
It moves when every file is on the same disk in a writable folder, or comes from the Trash; otherwise it copies.
The transfer goes through the same function a real drop calls, with progress and undo.
The menu item works from anywhere, even opened from the keyboard, and has no underlined letter.
The drag code now calls both shared functions, and the move fixes a small memory leak.
Without split view, a selection, focus in the file view, or a folder that takes the files, the key passes on.
Otherwise it moves on the same disk, copies across disks or from read-only folders, and moves into the Trash.
Files already in the other folder are skipped, and the rest still go.
In the drag code, about 40 lines became calls to the two shared functions.
lines.say: In the drag code, about forty lines became calls to the two shared functions.

lines.caption: The PR changes four source files and adds its test, this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert this PR; it stores no setting.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It reuses the drop rule and its refusal checks, the split-view code, and the function a real drop calls.
In this session it built twice in the cloud container, with no compiler warnings the first time.
The new test moved a file with Insert, left the location bar alone, and did nothing without split view.
The existing drag and drop test still passed, and all 12 tests passed.
lines.say: The existing drag and drop test still passed, and all twelve tests passed.

lines.caption: Not run: the copy case, moves into the Trash, the refusals, the focus rule and skipped files.
CI's own fix commit wasn't built or tested here; CI runs it.
A fresh review agent read the diff and the issue three times: 7 findings, then 4, then 2, all fixed or accepted.
lines.say: A fresh review agent read the diff and the issue three times: seven findings, then four, then two, all fixed or accepted.

lines.caption: The high one: the two extra keys would have taken over Paste and Copy, which led to keeping only Insert.
Fixed: refuse read-only folders and Trash subfolders, skip files already there, and drop the clashing underlined letter.
Accepted in round 2: the side pane's focus, the menu item's state, and the untested cases; CI's review fixed the first two.
Round 3 found two small ones about the menu item; one was fixed here, and CI fixed the other.
CI's own review ran twice at level high: 14 findings, 10 fixed and 4 accepted.
lines.say: C I's own review ran twice at level high: fourteen findings, ten fixed and four accepted.

lines.caption: Round 1's eight findings were all fixed but one, from the focus rule to sharing the drop's code.
In round 2, CI's own commit fixed three confirmed ones, including the keyboard-opened menu.
Accepted: a slow file lookup that never runs, because the selected files are always cached.
Accepted: Insert acts during type-ahead search, as Delete and Backspace do; GTK 3 can't tell the popup is open.
Also accepted: one refusal stays out of the shared check so drag and drop can't change, and no new doc comments.
CI builds and tests the final head with its own fix; copying across disks waits for a real desktop.
The changes, CI's comments and the issue are linked here.
Part 3. Nothing depends on issue 95.
lines.say: Part 3. Nothing depends on issue ninety-five.

lines.caption: Always-copy and always-move keys could come back under other keys, in a new issue, if you want them.
In short: in split view, Insert now sends the selection to the other pane, just as a drop would.
